lines.text: Retirement, by the way.
Very relaxing retirement.
I need Crons. I always need fucking Crons.
Please go.
FUCK.
Again.
Guardian smash remains a valid argument.
Why does this game have another currency?
Wrong storage.
Other wrong storage.
Found it.
My horse has more logistics than some companies.
I hate enhancement.
I am enhancing again.
BDO is beautiful right up until twelve menus open.
Ulukita feels like the game asking whether I've learned fear.
My family inventory has become a constitutional issue.
I'm impressed by how many systems BDO can fit inside a horse.
I swear every life skill has a secret graduate degree.
This outfit is clearly combat equipment because morale is a stat.
I'll never emotionally recover from learning another enhancement material exists.
There's a point where node knowledge becomes urban planning.
I'm not AFK. I'm spiritually supervising the horse.
BDO economy feels like several countries sharing one calculator.
My character can carry less than my determination expects.
I've become suspicious of any quest that says simple.
There are days when grinding is meditation with explosions.
I like combat systems that let me feel slightly dangerous at the keyboard.
If I ever fully understand contribution points, check on me.
A world boss is just a scheduled gathering of beautiful particle effects.
I've learned more about virtual shipping than I expected from retirement.
The horse is auto-running and somehow I'm still micromanaging.
I refuse to admit how long I've stared at marketplace graphs.
This game rewards planning and then places a shiny distraction twenty feet away.
I started with one character and immediately developed wardrobe policy.
Female characters only is still the easiest system in BDO.
I don't know who designed the storage rules, but I know they had enemies.
The ocean content is calling and I'm pretending not to hear it.
Every time I understand one menu, another menu becomes translucent in the distance.
My retirement plan now includes boss timers.
There's something peaceful about a long grind when nobody is talking nonsense.
I've enough materials to craft something. Which thing is still classified.
The beauty of BDO is occasionally interrupted by me opening twelve windows.
I'm deeply invested in a horse whose primary job is running in circles.
If the game asks me to sail, I'll somehow end up researching ship classes.
I respect any MMO willing to make cooking this complicated.
I came to stop leading people and accidentally found another giant world to organize.
Some days I want PvP. Some days I want to pick flowers in expensive armor.
The grind spot and I've entered a long-term relationship.
Nothing says retirement like optimizing fourteen hours of gameplay.
